_: THE connector catalogue, once: every card the Connections tab shows - the working ones (seeded as connector rows on first launch, store.py) and the planned ones - with a group, a one-line desc and `match`: the words in mail, chats, tasks and reports that mean this system. The tab reads it (connectorCatalog.js); the Advisor is handed the unconnected cards and judges which one the owner's threads are about (assistant.connect_evidence) - `match` decides nothing there any more.

sources._: Where work comes in: the groups whose working cards are a source of incoming work - mail, chat and task systems. Setup's Connect your main source offers them (email first, the usual one) and is done once one of them is connected and passes its test.

own_systems._: Systems the owner signs into that hold their own records - their databases and their books. A report source on one of these groups' cards is marked 'my own system' unless the owner turns it off, and a report run whose every source is marked is trusted (reports.is_own, origin.report_rests_on). Everything else - news, the web, social timelines, a free REST URL - starts unmarked.

actions._: WHAT THE OWNER PRESSES, PER CONNECTOR (the owner, 2026-11-05: "each connector should have settings what the action view looks like no?"). A card's `actions` lists the acts it can be set up for under a chat turn's Next steps, and one card (ActionCard.jsx) draws whatever is declared. Each: `kind` (post, email, chat, tracker), `road` (run_tool: a proposal on `tool`; reply: propose_reply / propose_email), the press words (`press`, `busy`, `done`, `undone`, `note`) and `fields`. A field has a `key` (the proposal's own), a `label` and a `type` (text, line, image, choice, people, files); `edit`: the owner may change it on the card before pressing; `agent`: the agent may propose it (general.roads tells it which); `setting`: a per-connection default on the Connections card, saved as default_<key> on the card and filled into the agent's proposal when it names none (connectorcatalog.with_defaults); a choice's own `press` / `busy` / `done` replace the act's while it is picked.

cards.title: Exchange Server
cards.desc: An on-premises Exchange mailbox over the server's IMAP and SMTP - in through triage, replies out from the same address, in-thread.

howto: Your Exchange server must have IMAP4 and authenticated SMTP switched on - ask IT for the host names (often mail.yourcompany.com; IMAP 993, SMTP 587).
Enter the mailbox address, the IMAP host and, if different, the SMTP host; paste the mailbox password (write-only).
An internal certificate the server signs itself shows its fingerprint on the first Test - paste it into TLS certificate only if IT confirms it.
Exchange Online / Microsoft 365 no longer takes IMAP passwords: use the Outlook card for those.

cards.title: Fastmail
cards.desc: A Fastmail mailbox over its own IMAP and SMTP - in through triage, replies out from the same address, in-thread.

preset.secret: app password (Fastmail: Settings → Privacy & Security → Integrations → New app password)
howto: Fastmail wants an app password, not your sign-in password: Settings → Privacy & Security → Integrations → New app password, access IMAP and SMTP.
Enter your Fastmail address and paste the app password (write-only) - the servers are already filled in.
Test logs in and adds the mailbox as a source; new mail flows in on the next sync, and replies you approve go out over Fastmail's SMTP.

cards.title: Proton Mail
cards.desc: A Proton Mail mailbox through Proton Mail Bridge, the app that runs on this computer - in through triage, replies out through the Bridge.

preset.secret: Bridge password (shown in Proton Mail Bridge, not your Proton password)
howto: Install Proton Mail Bridge on this computer (a paid Proton plan) and sign in to it - Proton's servers only speak to the Bridge, and Taskuary speaks to the Bridge.

In the Bridge, open your account's mailbox details: copy the user name (your address) and the Bridge password it shows. The ports are already filled in here (IMAP 1143, SMTP 1025, STARTTLS); change them only if you changed them in the Bridge.
The Bridge signs its connection with its own certificate, so the first Test names it and gives you its fingerprint - paste that into TLS certificate and Test again.
Mail flows in while the Bridge runs; replies you approve go out through it.

Enter your Yahoo address and paste the app password (write-only) - the servers are already filled in.
